---
title: "Interactive demos"
---

Every interactive demo in the course, in teaching order. Each one also appears in
its unit's exercise, together with questions to explore.

## Transforming an image with a 2×2 matrix

Drag the two columns of the matrix and watch the image follow. Unit: [Images as arrays & geometric transforms](images/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="demos/dist/demo.css">
<div data-demo="matrix2x2" data-mode="image" data-a="1 0 0 1"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/matrix2x2.js"></script>
```

## 3×3 kernels

Edit nine weights and see the filtered image live; click a pixel to see the weighted sum. Unit: [Filtering & convolution](kernels/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="kernel3x3" data-image="cell" data-preset="gauss"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/kernel3x3.js"></script>
```

## Build a wave from five frequencies

Unit: [Images in frequency space](fourier/exercise.qmd#explore-wave).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="fourierwave" data-a="1 0 0 0 0"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/fourierwave.js"></script>
```

## Filter an image in frequency space

Keep or remove parts of the 2D spectrum and see the image rebuilt. Unit: [Images in frequency space](fourier/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="fourier2d" data-mode="low" data-max="30"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/fourier2d.js"></script>
```

## The shape of a point cloud: PCA

Drag the points of a cloud of two-pixel images and a direction through it: centring, the covariance ellipse, the principal components, projection and reconstruction error. Unit: [Principal component analysis](pca/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="pca2d" data-data="pixels" data-angle="0"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/pca2d.js"></script>
```

## Smoothing before differentiating

A noisy 1D profile, its finite difference and its derivative-of-Gaussian response, with the kernel drawn to scale. Unit: [Edges: Gaussian derivatives and Canny](canny/exercise.qmd#explore-gaussderiv).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="gaussderiv" data-preset="noise"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/gaussderiv.js"></script>
```

## Canny step by step

Smoothing, gradient, non-maximum suppression and hysteresis, with a click-a-pixel inspector and the hysteresis flood replayed ring by ring. Unit: [Edges: Gaussian derivatives and Canny](canny/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="canny" data-preset="hyst"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/canny.js"></script>
```

## A 1D scale space

The blurred signal, slope or curvature for all σ at once, and each bump picking its own scale. Unit: [Scale space, blobs and pyramids](scale-space/exercise.qmd#explore-scale1d).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="scale1d" data-preset="bumps"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/scale1d.js"></script>
```

## Blobs over scales

Scale-normalised LoG and DoG blob detection in (x, y, σ), circles of radius √2·σ against the truth, and image pyramids. Unit: [Scale space, blobs and pyramids](scale-space/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="blobscale" data-preset="all"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/blobscale.js"></script>
```

## The Hessian per pixel

Eigenvalues of the Hessian classify every pixel as blob, ridge, saddle or flat; trace, determinant and multi-scale vesselness. Unit: [The Hessian: blobs, ridges and saddles](hessian/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="hessian" data-preset="hill"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/hessian.js"></script>
```

## The structure tensor

Orientation, coherence and corners from the averaged outer product of gradients, with the gradient cloud of any window. Unit: [The structure tensor](structure-tensor/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="structtensor" data-preset="edge"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/structtensor.js"></script>
```

## Quantisation and dithering

Round an image to 1–8 bits, with or without dither, and see the error and its histogram. Unit: [Quantisation & bit depth](quantisation/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="quantise" data-image="ramp" data-bits="4"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/quantise.js"></script>
```

## How many bits does a camera need?

A simulated camera (full well, read noise, ADC bits, exposure) and its noise-versus-signal plot. Unit: [Camera noise, SNR and PSNR](cameranoise/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="camerabits" data-fwc="30000" data-read="1.5" data-bits="16" data-exposure="0.5"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/camerabits.js"></script>
```

## Showing a 12-bit image: windows, wrap-around, CT windows

Unit: [12- and 16-bit images in practice](highbit/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="window16" data-image="fluo" data-preset="full"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/window16.js"></script>
```

## The bits of a float

Unit: [Floating point](floatingpoint/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="floatbits" data-format="float16" data-value="0.1"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/floatbits.js"></script>
```

## Summing many pixels in float32 and float16

Unit: [Floating point](floatingpoint/exercise.qmd#explore-sum).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="floatbits" data-view="sum" data-mean="1000" data-sd="50" data-n="22"></div>
```

## PSF and OTF of a microscope

Change the NA, the wavelength, defocus or motion and watch the PSF, the OTF with its cut-off 2NA/λ, and the blurred object. Unit: [Image formation and the point spread function](psf/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="psfotf" data-preset="oil"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/psfotf.js"></script>
```

## Two points on a pixel grid

Move two points together, change the pixel size and the photon count, and see when the dip disappears and when a grating aliases. Unit: [Resolution, sampling and measuring the PSF](resolution/exercise.qmd#explore-twopoints).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="resolve" data-preset="rayleigh"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/resolve.js"></script>
```

## The axial PSF: widefield and confocal

The xz slice of the 3D PSF, sampled with a z-step of your choice; the lateral and axial widths and the axial Nyquist step. Unit: [Resolution, sampling and measuring the PSF](resolution/exercise.qmd#explore-axial).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="resolve" data-mode="axial" data-preset="na14"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/resolve.js"></script>
```

## Measuring a PSF from beads

Average 1 to 30 noisy beads after background subtraction and sub-pixel centring, and compare the result with the true PSF. Unit: [Resolution, sampling and measuring the PSF](resolution/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="resolve" data-mode="beads" data-preset="one"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/resolve.js"></script>
```

## Deconvolution lab

Blur a test object, add noise and restore it with the inverse filter, a truncated inverse, Wiener or Tikhonov, reading each method from its gain curve. Unit: [Linear deconvolution](deconv/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="deconvlab" data-preset="wiener"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/deconvlab.js"></script>
```

## The regularisation path

A 1D profile restored with data term + λ · penalty (energy, roughness, total variation, non-negativity) or by stopping an iteration early, with the L-curve and the discrepancy principle. Unit: [Regularisation](regularise/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="regpath" data-preset="disc"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/regpath.js"></script>
```

## Richardson–Lucy step by step

Scrub through the iterations of Richardson–Lucy on photon-count data: semi-convergence, a forgotten background, a wrong PSF and blind deconvolution. Unit: [Richardson–Lucy, 3D, and the PSF](richardson-lucy/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="rlsteps" data-preset="semi"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/rlsteps.js"></script>
```

## 3D deconvolution and the missing cone

A widefield or confocal 3D stack restored with 3D Richardson–Lucy: beads sharpen in z, a horizontal sheet stays smeared. Unit: [Richardson–Lucy, 3D, and the PSF](richardson-lucy/exercise.qmd#explore-xz).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="rlsteps" data-mode="xz" data-preset="bead"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/rlsteps.js"></script>
```

## Denoisers compared

Gaussian, median, bilateral, non-local means and Wiener, each judged by what it destroys, with the method noise. Unit: [Denoising and what you may measure](denoise/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="denoisers" data-preset="gaussstep"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/denoisers.js"></script>
```

## What may be measured after restoration

A field with known truth: integrated intensities hold, while peaks, sizes, separations and counts change with the restoration. Unit: [Denoising and what you may measure](denoise/exercise.qmd#explore-measure).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="rlsteps" data-mode="measure" data-preset="integrals"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/rlsteps.js"></script>
```

## Histogram and a global threshold

Drag a threshold over the histogram, add noise and smoothing, and watch the mask and its area change. Unit: [Histograms & a global threshold](histogram/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="histthresh" data-preset="clean"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/histthresh.js"></script>
```

## Otsu by hand

Drag the bars of an 8-level histogram and watch the between-class variance table and the isodata steps. Unit: [Choosing the threshold](otsu/exercise.qmd#explore-otsubars).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="otsubars" data-preset="example"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/otsubars.js"></script>
```

## Two Gaussians, six thresholds

Compare Otsu, isodata, minimum error, triangle, maximum entropy and the Bayes boundary on a two-class mixture. Unit: [Choosing the threshold](otsu/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="mixture" data-preset="weights"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/mixture.js"></script>
```

## Local thresholds under uneven illumination

Global Otsu, background division, mean − C, Niblack and Sauvola on a shaded image with ground truth. Unit: [Local thresholds & hysteresis](local-threshold/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="localthresh" data-preset="global"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/localthresh.js"></script>
```

## Hysteresis thresholding

Two thresholds, keeping only what is connected to a sure seed: in 1D and on faint filaments. Unit: [Local thresholds & hysteresis](local-threshold/exercise.qmd#explore-hysteresis).

```{=html}
<div data-demo="hysteresis" data-preset="hyst"></div>
<script src="demos/dist/hysteresis.js"></script>
```

## ROC and precision–recall

Confusion matrix, Dice and the ROC and precision–recall curves of a threshold sweep against ground truth. Unit: [Evaluation against ground truth](seg-eval/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}

<script src="demos/dist/threshroc.js"></script>
```

## From a spectrum to three numbers

Draw a spectrum and see what the eye, a camera or a colour-blind viewer makes of it; make metamers and watch them break under another lamp. Unit: [From a spectrum to three numbers](colour-vision/exercise.qmd#explore).

Mix two lights on the xy diagram, or design a display from three primaries and a white point. Unit: [From a spectrum to three numbers](colour-vision/exercise.qmd#explore-chromaticity).

The same blur or downsampling on gamma-encoded codes and in linear light: 128 or 188? Unit: [RGB: gamma, linear maps and white balance](rgb-linear/exercise.qmd#explore).

Y′CbCr with chroma subsampling, greyscale as a choice of weights, and any 3×3 matrix on linear RGB. Unit: [RGB: gamma, linear maps and white balance](rgb-linear/exercise.qmd#explore-matrix).

<script src="demos/dist/whitebalance.js"></script>

An image's pixels as a rotatable 3D point cloud that morphs between sRGB, linear RGB, XYZ, Y′CbCr, HSV and CIELAB. Unit: [HSV, CIELAB and colour segmentation](colour-perceptual/exercise.qmd#explore).

<div data-demo="colourcloud" data-preset="hsv"></div>

RGB thresholds, a hue wedge, a ΔE ball, Otsu on one channel or k-means: which space makes the red apple a simple region? Unit: [HSV, CIELAB and colour segmentation](colour-perceptual/exercise.qmd#explore-seg).

<div data-demo="colourseg" data-preset="rgb"></div>

Jet versus viridis with the lightness profile underneath, diverging maps for signed data, channel merges and a dichromat simulation. Unit: [Colour for display](colour-display/exercise.qmd#explore).

Six cells with the same mask and the same total signal. Change the background offset, gain, noise, saturation and mask error, and watch the mean, median, MAD, edge/mean ratio, mass displacement and radial rings respond. The population and plate tabs add per-well aggregation and robust z normalisation. Unit: [Intensity inside an object](intensity-features/exercise.qmd#explore).

```{=html}

<script src="demos/dist/intensityfeat.js"></script>
```
